study: Guest-only checkout friction teardown — grocery/marketplace competitors
method: Browserbase advanced-stealth + residential-proxy sessions, market pinned to Atlanta GA (proxy resolves to metro level, not exact zip), driven live via browse CLI by parallel agents. No accounts, no orders placed.
headline_finding: NONE of the four competitors offer true guest checkout. Every one forces account creation before the payment step is reachable. This means (a) forced-account is the dominant new-user friction metric, and (b) payment-method matrices for these sites require authenticated sessions — the logged-in phase.

forced_account_ranking_worst_to_least.note: Hardest — tiles read 'Sign In to Add'; /cart redirects to login. Guest cannot even build a cart or see a subtotal.
Can build cart + see subtotal as guest; 'Proceed to checkout' redirects to /ap/signin in one click. No guest option.
Can build a persistent cart; login modal fires on 'View Cart'. Itemized fees gated behind login.
Only CTA is 'Sign in to check out'; unrecognized email escalates to forced 'Create an account' (first/last name + passkey/password). Also $35 shipping minimum.

payment_methods_matrix.note: Guest sessions could only fully observe Instacart (via public help pages). Amazon/Target/Kroger payment methods sit behind the account wall and need the logged-in phase to verify directly; values below marked 'auth-gated' were not observable as a guest.

instacart.own_wallet: Instacart Card Network (Pay with Points), OTC Network card

payment_methods_matrix.amazon: auth-gated (footer references Amazon Visa/Store Card/Secured/Business + Shop with Points; historically Affirm BNPL, EBT/SNAP on Fresh, HSA/FSA, no Apple/Google Pay/PayPal — verify logged-in)
payment_methods_matrix.target: auth-gated (historically all cards, Target Wallet, Apple/Google/Samsung Pay, PayPal, Affirm/Afterpay/Klarna/Sezzle/Zip, HSA/FSA; EBT in-store only — verify logged-in)
payment_methods_matrix.kroger: auth-gated (historically cards, Kroger Pay, PayPal, EBT/SNAP online; no Apple/Google Pay online; HSA/FSA pharmacy-only — verify logged-in)

ebt_signal_pre_auth.note: EBT/SNAP eligibility is surfaced on product tiles BEFORE login on the grocery sites — a capturable payments signal even guest-only.
ebt_signal_pre_auth.target: All milk tiles tagged 'SNAP EBT eligible'
ebt_signal_pre_auth.kroger: Milk tiles carry 'SNAP EBT' labels + inline digital coupons
ebt_signal_pre_auth.instacart: SNAP-Eligible filter chip; Costco warehouse items not individually flagged
ebt_signal_pre_auth.amazon: Not shown on the non-grocery items sampled

prices_sampled_whole_milk_1gal.note: Different markets/pack sizes; illustrative only, not a like-for-like price comparison

market_geo_caveat: Browserbase geo proxies pin to metro level, not exact zip. Target resolved to Jacksonville FL 32224; Amazon 30318, Kroger ~30306, Instacart 30039 (Atlanta metro). For a published benchmark, either accept metro-level or set the delivery address explicitly in the logged-in phase.
implication_for_next_phase: Logged-in phase is REQUIRED to complete the payment-methods matrix and the field-count/steps-to-purchase metrics for Amazon, Target, Kroger — all three wall the payment screen behind an account. Instacart's methods are already documented. The forced-account ranking above is a finished, publishable friction finding on its own.
